findings.description: `float line = ...` uses `line` as a variable name. In HLSL `line` is a reserved keyword (a geometry-shader primitive type, like point/triangle/lineadj). fxc, which Unity uses for d3d11 and as the front end of the HLSLcc cross-compile, fails with "syntax error: unexpected token 'line'". GLSL allows the name, which is why the JS code works. The result is that the VoxelForge/TerrainXray shader does not compile. matXray1 and matXray2 then fall back to the error shader, so X-Ray mode draws all terrain magenta or not at all.
findings.suggestedFix: Rename the local, e.g. `float edgeLine = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, w, mid); if (edgeLine < 0.04) discard; return float4(t.rgb * (0.5 + 0.5 * i.sad.x), edgeLine * 0.42);`

findings.description: In X-Ray mode JS draws entities with GL_DEPTH_TEST disabled. Disabling the depth test also turns off depth writes, so mobs leave no depth behind. The Unity port gets 'Always' by setting matEntityXray to ZTest Always, but the shader hard-codes `ZWrite On`, so X-Ray mobs still write depth. Everything drawn later with a depth test is then cut out behind mob silhouettes: mob-held items, drops, translucent terrain, water, clouds and the selection outline. In JS those draw over the X-Ray mobs, because after the X-Ray depth clear the depth buffer holds only ore/special blocks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `_ZWrite ("ZWrite", Float) = 1` to Properties and use `ZWrite [_ZWrite]` in the pass. Then in VF.Renderer.cs set `m.SetFloat("_ZWrite", 0)` for matEntityXray and keep 1 for matEntity.

findings.jsRef: drawMainClouds (pretty.js 17370-17390; depthFunc is LESS, restored after the water colour pass at 27057)
findings.description: The cloud pass uses `ZTest LEqual`. In JS the depth function is LESS when drawMainClouds runs (the water colour pass sets it back to LESS before clouds), so fragments at exactly equal depth are rejected in JS but accepted in the port.
findings.suggestedFix: Change to `ZTest Less`.

reviews.coverageNotes:
I read all 9 shaders and VFCommon.cginc, plus the context files VF.Renderer.cs (materials, render-state floats, globals, draw order), VF.ChunkRender.cs (TERRAIN_LAYOUT), VF.DynMesh.cs (SPRITE/PARTICLE layouts) and VF.Atlas.cs (texture array and mips). I compared each shader against its JS program: terrainProg, terrainOpaqueFastProg, terrainXrayProg, waterProg, waterDepthProg, lineProg, entityProg, dropProg, cloudProg and breakParticleProg.

I also traced GL state at each draw in JS render(): sky bodies, X-Ray passes 1 and 2 with the depth clear, opaque fast and cutout, break particles, entities and mob-held items, active entities, fishing line, drops, cracks, translucent terrain, water above and below the surface (depth pre-pass plus LEQUAL colour pass), clouds, selection outline, primed-TNT outline, and held items.

These all match, apart from the three findings:
- **Shader math:** shade/alpha/class decode, sky:block light decode with the hand-light term, the lightmap coordinates (block on x, sky on y), fog smoothstep, underwater tint (`_VF_FogFar > 30`), and the alpha-test thresholds (0.12 / 0.08 / 0.01).
- **Atlas sampling:** the mip-LOD formula and the NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR emulation (floor/frac blend, clamped to level 4). The C# array has 5 mips with point filtering and a single 768-layer page, so the JS 3-page split is correctly merged.
- **Other math:** water flow-tile UV animation, the X-Ray edge-line maths, the entity 4x7 grid UVs and the sprite grid UVs with the 1-f.y flip.
- **Interpolation:** flat (nointerpolation) qualifiers.
- **Vertex inputs:** semantics match the C# layouts — terrain uses Float16 UV, Float32 packed shade/alpha and Float16 tile/light (all exact for the value ranges); sprite and entity use 7 floats; particles use 11 floats.
- **Uniforms:** every property and global name C# sets (_VF_*, _Cull/_SrcBlend/_DstBlend/_ZTest/_ZWrite, _Grid, _NoFog, _XrayMode, _WaterPass, _Color, _MainTex, _VF_CloudOff) is declared.
- **Render state:** each material's Cull/ZTest/ZWrite/Blend matches the JS GL state, except entity X-Ray (SHD-2) and clouds (SHD-3).

Platform checks: I checked HLSL reserved words in every shader (only `line` collides), the UnityObjectToClipPos float4 overload, the 2darray/target 3.5 requirements, ddx/ddy sign independence (only squared magnitudes are used), reversed-Z handling of property-driven ZTest, and gamma-space parity (no sRGB conversions involved).

Not verifiable offline: I could not run a real Unity shader compile, because the stub compile check only covers C#. I also did not report one cross-subsystem doubt. JS uploads the lightmap with texSubImage2D while UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL is still left true after image loads, which in some browsers would flip the lightmap rows. Whether that happens depends on the browser, and since the rest of the game would only look right without the flip, I treated it as out of scope.

findings.description: In X-ray mode the JS turns DEPTH_TEST off entirely for the entity draw. In GL that also stops depth writes, so the entities leave the depth buffer untouched. The port only sets _ZTest=Always on matEntityXray, and VFEntity.shader hardcodes 'ZWrite On', so X-ray entities still write depth. Everything drawn after them (mob held items, active entities, drops, cracks, translucent terrain, water, the selection outline) is then depth-tested against the entity silhouettes. Water or glass that sits behind a mob but in front of the terrain is hidden in Unity, while in JS it is drawn over the mob.
findings.suggestedFix: Turn depth writes off for the X-ray entity material. Add a `_ZWrite ("ZWrite", Float) = 1` property to VFEntity.shader and use `ZWrite [_ZWrite]` (the shader file is owned elsewhere). Then initialise matEntityXray with m.SetFloat("_ZWrite", 0) next to _ZTest=Always.

findings.description: buildOpaqueRenderList calls chunkRenderRegionKey(c.cx, c.cz) once for every opaque-visible chunk on every frame. That is `rx + "," + rz`: two int boxings plus a string.Concat, then a string-hash Dictionary lookup. At render distance 10-16, that means hundreds to a thousand-plus visible chunks, i.e. roughly 3 heap allocations each, every frame. That is tens of KB of garbage per frame on the hottest render path, which causes periodic GC spikes and works against the fastest-rendering goal.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid building strings per frame. Either cache the RenderRegion reference on the Chunk (look it up from renderRegions once, invalidated when cleanupRenderRegions or getRenderRegion replaces the entry), or keep a parallel Dictionary<long, RenderRegion> keyed by ((long)rx << 32) | (uint)rz for the hot lookup.

findings.description: JS Array.prototype.sort is stable. List<T>.Sort(Comparison) is an unstable introsort, and it also allocates a comparer wrapper on every call. When two chunks have equal _renderDist2 (e.g. mirrored dx/dz offsets when the eye's fractional x and z positions match), their relative order differs from JS and can change from frame to frame. transRenderList (reverse visible order) and waterRenderList (front-to-back) take their draw order from this list, so overlapping translucent or water chunks with tied distances can blend in a different order or flicker. The port conventions require a stable sort wherever JS uses Array.sort.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a stable sort. The list is almost sorted from frame to frame, so a hand-written insertion sort on _renderDist2 is both stable and allocation-free. Alternatively, tie-break on the original index captured before sorting.

findings.jsRef: uploadAndDrawDrops / ensureDropIndexQuads (pretty.js 16674-16860): grow-only bufferData + bufferSubData, index pattern uploaded only when capacity grows
findings.description: Every frame, DynMesh.Upload calls SetVertexBufferParams(vn) and SetIndexBufferParams(ic) with the exact current counts for each of about 15 dynamic meshes. Those counts change almost every frame (sky, entities, drops, particles, lines, held items), so Unity reallocates the GPU vertex and index buffers each frame. The constant quad index pattern (0,1,2,2,1,3 per quad) is also re-uploaded every frame; for the entity batch that is 6 ints per quad. The JS keeps grow-only GPU capacity, uploads with bufferSubData, and uploads the quad index buffer only when its capacity grows. lastIndexCount is tracked but never used to skip any work.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep a vertex capacity and an index capacity, and call Set*BufferParams only when the needed size exceeds them (grow by doubling). Upload vertices with SetVertexBufferData(data, 0, 0, vn*floatsPerVert). For quad meshes, upload the static index pattern once per capacity change. Then call SetSubMesh(0, new SubMeshDescriptor(0, ic, topo){ firstVertex = 0, vertexCount = vn, bounds = ... }, MUF) so that only the used range is drawn.

findings.description: recycleMesh pushes freed chunk and region meshes into meshPool (up to 256) with their full vertex and index buffers still allocated, both the GPU buffers and Unity's CPU-side copy. The JS frees GL buffers at once. After the render distance drops, a teleport, or mass chunk unloads, up to 256 meshes stay resident. Some of these are 2x2 region meshes holding tens of thousands of vertices at 24 B each, plus indices. That can hold hundreds of MB that nothing uses. Reuse also gives no buffer benefit, because writeTerrainMesh always calls SetVertexBufferParams and SetIndexBufferParams with new sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Call m.Clear() before pushing a mesh into the pool, so only the managed Mesh object is reused and its buffers are released. Also consider a much smaller cap (e.g. 32), or destroying meshes above a byte budget.

findings.description: In JS, dp is ImageData.data, a Uint8ClampedArray. Assigning a fractional value like (r/tw)*0.8 + sp[base]*0.2 to it rounds to the nearest integer (ties to even). The C# port casts with (byte)Math.Max(0, Math.Min(255, v)) at lines 75-78, which truncates toward zero. Every RGB and alpha texel of the runtime flowing-water tile (WATER_FLOW_TILE, mip level 0 and the mips built from it) comes out about 0.5 LSB darker or more transparent than the reference, and up to 1 LSB off per channel.
findings.suggestedFix: Round the way Uint8ClampedArray does: (byte)Math.Max(0, Math.Min(255, Math.Round(v, MidpointRounding.ToEven))) for all four channels.

findings.description: buildMainActiveEntities runs every frame and allocates on the heap on its hot path. renderVehicleBox creates a capturing Func closure plus 24 double[3] (renderVehiclePoint) and 6 double[][] (Q) per box. renderVehiclePrismMain allocates double[8][] plus 8 points and 6 Q arrays. renderBoatOarMain allocates c0/c1/c2 and 6 mul3 arrays plus a closure. addMainArrow allocates bases plus 2x(double[4][] + 4 points) per arrow. One boat costs about 250 allocations per frame and a minecart about 150, so the GC churns continuously while vehicles or arrows are loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Transform the corners into stack locals (or a static reusable double[8][3] scratch) and push through P4/fxPts. Replace the Func/mul3 closures with inline math. Keep static scratch arrays for the prism corners and the arrow quad.

findings.description: appendSelectionBox allocates 9 arrays (an outer array plus 8 corner double[3]) per box, and buildSelectionOutline calls it every frame whenever a block is targeted. buildPrimedOutlines also allocates a new double[6] per primed TNT per frame (line 220). These are steady per-frame GC allocations on the overlay path.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit the 12 edges directly from x0..z1 locals with lineSeg (or use a static double[8][3] scratch). Hoist the primed box bounds into a static readonly double[] { -0.05, -0.05, -0.05, 1.05, 1.05, 1.05 }.

findings.description: buildFirstPersonHeld runs every frame in first person and allocates for each held item. hId/hT/hS/hRX/hRY/hRZ/hMX each allocate a float[16], and every hMul allocates another one, so a block uses about 10 matrices and the bow about 12. heldBoundsForKey also allocates a HeldBounds plus 2 double[]. With the off-hand filled that is 25-30 allocations per frame (Array.Copy into g.matrix already makes the temporaries redundant).
findings.suggestedFix: Keep a few static float[16] scratch matrices and compose in place: an hMulInto(dst, a, b) helper and setters that fill preallocated buffers. Return the bounds through out-parameters or static readonly HeldBounds instances, since the bounds are constants.

findings.description: buildMainSkyBodies creates a new capturing Action delegate and closure every frame (it captures ex/ey/ez). buildFishingLine allocates double[11][] plus 11 double[3] every frame while fishing (lines 241-242). mainSkyState allocates a SkyState and a double[3] on each call, and the renderer calls it every frame. All of this is avoidable per-frame garbage.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the sky 'add' a static method that takes ex/ey/ez parameters. Compute the fishing-line points into a static double[33] scratch, or emit segments from the previous point kept in locals. Reuse one static SkyState and its sky array, since callers use the result immediately.

findings.description: minimapColor allocates a capturing Func<double,byte> closure (it captures shade) on every call, which is 256 allocations per rebuilt chunk. In updateMinimap, spawnKey is rebuilt every frame (line 146) with Array.ConvertAll, a lambda, JS.ToStr strings and string.Join, even when nothing changed. The rot lambda and P0..P3 arrays (lines 180-181) are allocated on every redraw.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline the clamp/round into a static helper byte mmClamp(double v, double shade). Build spawnKey only when player.spawn's rounded values differ from cached doubles. Compute the arrow corners into locals.

findings.description: buildEntityBatch runs every frame and allocates on this path. getWorldLight allocates a double[2] for each rendered mob plus the third-person player. skeletonHandAt allocates a double[3], and addSkeletonBow allocates double[4][] plus 4 points per skeleton per frame. addThirdPersonHeld allocates 5 arrays per frame. The rest of the batch path was written to be allocation-free, and these calls undo that with steady GC churn.
findings.suggestedFix: Have entityLight decode the packed light inline (sky=(p>>4)&15, blk=p&15) instead of calling getWorldLight. Return the skeleton hand through out-parameters. Use a static double[4][3] scratch for the bow and held-item quads passed to dropPushQuad.

findings.description: `new Section { blocks = q.blocks, light = light }` is an object initializer, so it first runs the parameterless Section() constructor (World/Types.cs:11). That constructor allocates two new 4096-byte arrays and fills light with 0xf0 in a 4096-step loop, and then both arrays are overwritten at once. Every generated chunk can have up to 24 sections, so each integrateGenResult throws away about 200 KB and runs about 100k extra loop steps on the main thread. This happens inside stream()'s time-budgeted gen-integration loop, up to 2 times per frame, and it inflates avgGenIntegrateMs.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the existing two-argument constructor: `sections[q.si] = new Section(q.blocks, light);`

findings.jsRef: titleMenu onclick -> location.reload() (pretty.js ~27170); `let day = 0.18` (25603); player literal (16253)
findings.description: returnToTitle() stands in for location.reload() but does not reset session state that a reload re-initialises. `day` keeps its value. loadGame() only restores day when a save with a "day" field exists (Game/VF.Inventory.cs:316), so a brand-new world started after 'Выбор режима' begins at the previous session's time of day instead of 0.18. In the same way, player.yaw/pitch/camMode and xrayActive carry over into the next world, whereas JS starts from the player literal's defaults.
findings.suggestedFix: In returnToTitle reset `day = 0.18`, `player.yaw = player.pitch = 0`, `player.camMode = 0`, `xrayActive = false`, and the interactionPrev* NaN sentinels (and optionally streamCleanupIter = null, queue.Clear()), matching the JS initial values.

findings.description: JS terminates the worker on failure. In C#, failWorkerEngine only does genSlots.Clear() and never sets slot.stop or signals slot.ev. The mesh-error path in drainWorkerMessages (line 219) also only sets slot.alive=false. The affected threads stay blocked in ev.WaitOne() forever, each holding its WorldGenKernel or MeshCore (region and vertex scratch buffers). returnToTitle -> shutdownWorkerEngine never reaches them because they were already removed from genSlots, or are still in meshSlots but dead. Each failure and restart cycle leaks threads and memory, and the AutoResetEvents are never disposed.
findings.suggestedFix: In failWorkerEngine, before clearing, do `foreach (var s in genSlots) { s.stop = true; s.ev.Set(); }`. In the mesh error branch, set `slot.stop = true; slot.ev.Set();`. Optionally Dispose the events once the threads exit.

findings.description: prioritizeWorkerQueues re-sorts genJobs/meshJobs with LINQ `OrderBy(...).ToList()` and then Clear/AddRange. While streaming it runs 3 times per frame (stream line 236, fillGenJobsMain line 183, stream line 271), plus the extra meshJobs OrderBy at line 295. Every call allocates an OrderedEnumerable, key and index buffers and a new List, and calls streamPriority twice per element. This is steady per-frame GC pressure in the hottest scheduling path. JS sorts the arrays in place.
findings.suggestedFix: Sort in place with a stable insertion sort keyed on streamPriority. The lists are short (at most GEN_QUEUE_LIMIT) and mostly already sorted, so this is cheap and allocation-free. Alternatively, precompute keys into a reusable int[] and do a stable index sort.

I read all four engine files in full and compared them against pretty.js.

findings.description: In full mode JS appends every section straight into one chunk-level aggregate (`buildSection(si, metaMap, agg)` gives secLens) and the per-section geometry is only subarray views into that aggregate, so each vertex is copied once. C# copies each section's VBuf/IBuf into new per-section arrays in take() (and worldifies them there), then copies all of them again into aggO/C/W/T in concat() (lines 1099-1101). So every full mesh, which is the common case while streaming, allocates and copies its whole vertex and index data twice on the mesher thread. That doubles the transient garbage per chunk, and with Unity's stop-the-world GC this garbage also stalls the main thread.
findings.suggestedFix: In full mode, write all sections into chunk-level VBuf/IBuf (the way JS uses agg) and record per-section offsets and lengths. Build aggO..aggT once from those, worldifying a single time. Then either give GeoBucket an (array, offset, count) view so full24[si] points into the aggregate arrays, or make the per-section copies from the aggregate, so that only one of the two copies is a full allocation.

findings.description: Several hot per-block paths allocate on the heap every time they run. stairBoxesMain allocates 3 Func delegates plus a closure, 2-3 Lists and the rotateBox clones for every stair block (lines 731-758). emitRail allocates a Func closure for every sloped rail (line 910). shapeBoxes and vShapeBoxes allocate a new List and new double[] for every slab, gate, trapdoor or plate. flushFlatWaterTops allocates a List, a Dictionary and one List per group for every section that contains water (lines 586-592). Villages, structures and oceans produce thousands of these objects per chunk on the mesher threads, and that garbage adds to Unity's stop-the-world GC pauses, which also stop the main thread.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the stair helpers (metaAt/isStair/guard) and the rail `up` lambda private methods that take their parameters directly. Return cached static box arrays for fixed shapes such as slab top/bottom, carpet, plate and pot, or write boxes into a reusable per-instance List<double[]>. For flat water, keep per-instance pooled group lists and a reusable Dictionary that is cleared at the start of each flush.

findings.jsRef: clearRuntimeWorld / scheduleWorldSave / saveWorldNow (pretty.js 4406-4434, 4507-4521); in JS the page reload kills any pending setTimeout
findings.description: In JS, leaving a world reloads the page, so a pending scheduleWorldSave timer can never fire afterwards. In the port, returnToTitle() (VF.Frame.cs) calls saveGameNow() and then clearRuntimeWorld(). clearRuntimeWorld() empties edits, editsByChunk and blockMeta, but it never cancels saveTimer (VF.World.cs:272/287), and Timers.Tick() keeps running on the title screen (VoxelForgeGame.Update). Many background ticks call scheduleWorldSave: fluidBreakCrossPlant -> addEditIndex(save=true), setBlock with persist from crops, farmland, fire, leaf decay, and obsidian/cobble/stone from setFluidBlock. So a 300 ms timer is often pending when the player quits. When it fires, saveWorldNow() runs with SAVE_KEYS still set to the old world (keys only change in configureSaveMode) and with empty edits/meta. It writes {seed, edits:[], meta:[]} over the world's save, and every block the player placed or broke is lost. The same pattern exists for saveGameT/saveStateNow in VF.Inventory.cs.
findings.suggestedFix: In clearRuntimeWorld(), call Timers.clearTimeout(saveTimer); saveTimer = 0; first. returnToTitle has already called saveGameNow, so nothing is lost. Ask the Inventory owner to cancel saveGameT the same way in returnToTitle/resetContainers.

findings.jsRef: tickPressurePlates (pretty.js 20498-20520): for (const q of worldDrops) ... - a live JS array iteration that tolerates push
findings.description: tickPressurePlates uses a C# foreach over worldDrops (a List<WorldDrop>). A drop on a wooden plate calls touchPressurePlate -> primePlateTNT -> setBlock(TNT -> AIR) -> validateAttachmentsAround -> detachUnsupportedAt. In survival, detachUnsupportedAt calls spawnWorldDrop (VF.BlockRules.cs:453/468), which does worldDrops.Add. On the next MoveNext the foreach throws InvalidOperationException ('Collection was modified'). That aborts the rest of tickWorldDynamics and the frame's Update. Repro: a torch, button, or other attachment on a TNT block within 3x3x4 under a wooden pressure plate, and an item dropped onto the plate. JS keeps iterating with no error.
findings.suggestedFix: Iterate by index, as JS for-of over a growing array does: for (int i = 0; i < worldDrops.Count; i++) { var q = worldDrops[i]; scanPlateUnderEntity(q.x, q.y, q.z, 0.1, false, now); }. Index the liveMobs loop the same way for safety.

findings.jsRef: snapshotSimMap / tickFire / tickFurnaces (pretty.js ~4850, 20311, 20533) - JS reuses the global simEntryKeys/simEntryVals scratch arrays
findings.description: snapshotSimMap() builds a new List<KeyValuePair> on every call. tickFire calls it every frame even when worldSim.fires is empty, which allocates a List plus the OrderedMap enumerator. tickFurnaces (line 617) also allocates new List<KeyValuePair<string,Furnace>>(furnaces) every frame, and tickFallingBlocks (line 473) does OrderBy(...).ToList() every frame while more than one block is falling. JS avoids these per-frame allocations by reusing scratch arrays, so the port adds steady GC pressure in the hot game loop.
findings.suggestedFix: Return early from tickFire when worldSim.fires.Count == 0, and from tickFurnaces when furnaces.Count == 0. Snapshot into reusable static scratch lists (one per caller, since the calls are not nested), cleared before each use. For falling blocks, sort in place with a stable insertion sort on y, or skip the sort when the list is already ordered.

findings.jsRef: caveBiomeAt wrapper (pretty.js 12081) and kernel caveBiomeAt (9267); caller pretty.js 26423 caveBiomeAt(player.x, Math.floor(player.y), player.z)
findings.description: The JS ambient cave-biome query passes the fractional player.x/player.z. The kernel samples valueNoise3Main(x*0.018 ..., z*0.018 ...) at those unfloored coordinates. The C# wrapper only accepts ints, so the caller in VF.Frame.cs:122 floors x and z first. The lush, dripstone and deep-dark noise is then sampled at different points, so the ambient cave biome (fog, music, environment) flips at slightly different positions near biome borders than in JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a double overload, caveBiomeAt(double x, double y, double z, int? h = null), that forwards unfloored x/z to the kernel noise sampling (the surface lookup inside can still floor). This needs a matching double entry point in WorldGenKernel.caveBiomeAt.

findings.jsRef: SHIP_ALL / SHIP_BEACHABLE / weightedPrefix / SHIP_ALL_WEIGHT (pretty.js ~10620-10632), which are module constants built once when the kernel is created
findings.description: ensureShipTables() fills static fields lazily without a lock or memory barrier. Several VF-Gen threads start at the same moment and reach structureCandidate() for their first chunks almost together. A thread can see SHIP_ALL as non-null and return early, even though another thread's earlier stores to SHIP_ALL_WEIGHT, SHIP_BEACH_WEIGHT and SHIP_BEACHABLE are not yet visible to it. Stores are reordered like this on ARM64 under IL2CPP and Mono (Android, iOS, Apple Silicon). weightedShip() then dereferences a null prefix array, throws NullReferenceException in GenWorker.Run, and failWorkerEngine stops all chunk generation. On x86 the window is harmless. In JS these tables are built once, synchronously.
findings.suggestedFix: Build the four tables in GenData.Build(), which runs on the main thread before any worker starts, and store them as static fields there. Or guard ensureShipTables with a lock or Volatile.Write and publish SHIP_ALL last with a release store. Then remove the lazy call from structureCandidate.

findings.jsRef: ravinesForChunk / planRavine / structureCandidate / mineshaftsForChunk string keys (pretty.js ~9455-9475, ~10690, ~11143)
findings.description: Hot cache lookups build a fresh string key on every call: `seed + ":" + cx + "," + cz` boxes three ints and allocates the concatenated string. This happens in ravinesForChunk (reached from ravineContains2D for every landPlantInfoAt and featureKindAt that produces a feature), planRavine (169 times per ravinesForChunk miss), structureCandidate, mineshaftsForChunk and planMineshaft (361 times per miss). nearbyStructures also allocates a List on each call, and surfaceStructureReservedAt calls it 4 times per feature column. In generateDense this runs for 256 surface columns plus the 26x26 feature ring, so each chunk produces thousands of short-lived objects. The output matches JS. The problem is cost in Unity: its Boehm GC stops every thread, so garbage from the generator threads causes main-thread frame hitches while streaming.
findings.suggestedFix: Key these Dictionaries on a long built from the two ints, for example ((long)cx << 32) | (uint)cz. The seed prefix is unneeded because setSeed already clears every cache. Have nearbyStructures fill a reusable per-kernel List, or let surfaceStructureReservedAt test candidates inline. Lookup order and results stay the same.

findings.description: In JS, the heap's sift-up compares the stored Float32 parent key against the caller's unrounded double f (`if (mobPathHeapF[p] <= f) break;`). Only the stored copy is rounded to float32. The C# version rounds f to float before the loop (`float f = (float)fd;`) and compares with that rounded value. Take a new node whose double f is slightly below its parent's float32 key but rounds to the same float32. JS swaps it upward and C# stops (P <= P). That changes which node pops next among near-equal f values, so A* can expand nodes in a different order and occasionally return a different path or best-partial node than the reference.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the double for the comparison and store the float: `mobPathHeap[i] = idx; mobPathHeapF[i] = (float)fd; while (i > 0) { int p = (i - 1) >> 1; if (mobPathHeapF[p] <= fd) break; ...; mobPathHeapF[i] = (float)fd; }`.

findings.description: mobSwimPhysics builds a capturing lambda (`Func<double,double,double,bool> can`, which captures m and wasWater) on every call. This runs for every aquatic mob on every 50 ms fixed step, and also on dry-land hops through updateAquaticSource. With up to 40 fish plus sharks that is about 800+ closure and delegate allocations per second (more when the loop catches up with up to 3 steps per frame), which adds avoidable GC pressure in a hot path. The JS arrow allocates too, but in Unity's Mono GC this costs more.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the lambda with a static helper, for example `static bool mobSwimCan(Mob m, bool wasWater, double x, double y, double z) { return mobSpaceClear(x, y, z, m) && (!wasWater || mobWaterLike(mobLoadedBlock(x, y + 0.05, z))); }`, and call it directly at the three call sites.

findings.description: stairsBoxesMainSync creates three Func delegates (isStair, mm, guard) plus a closure object, and allocates `new JObj()` for each missing neighbour meta, every time it runs. collisionBoxesAt -> specialShapeBoxes(stairs) calls it once per stair cell inside every playerCollisionAt scan. movePlayer runs 3+ such scans per substep (one per axis, the 0.6 step-up probe and its 0.05 descent loop of up to 12 probes), and mob collision (VF.Mobs.cs:420) uses the same path. Walking on or next to stairs therefore makes dozens of short-lived delegate and closure objects per frame, which is GC churn in the hottest physics path. The same pattern hits recoverPlayerOverlapSource (line 336): it captures ox/oy/oz in the tryNudge lambda, so the closure display class is allocated on every movePlayer substep even when there is no overlap.
findings.suggestedFix: Turn the stairs lambdas into private static helpers that take (x, y, z) as parameters, e.g. static bool stairAt(int x,int y,int z) and static JObj stairMeta(int x,int y,int z) that return a shared static empty JObj, and inline guard as a static method. In recoverPlayerOverlapSource, make tryNudge a static method that takes ox/oz, or create the lambda only after the early 'no overlap' return, so the common path allocates nothing.

findings.description: Each vehicle allocates several heap arrays every frame. vehicleBlocked loops over `new[] { -0.8, 0.8 }` and `new[] { -0.5, 0.5 }`, or over a 5-array jagged literal for minecarts (line 119), and is called twice per boat per frame. railYNear (line 75) allocates `new[] {0,1,-1,2,-2}`. railConnections (lines 80-83) allocates a List, a `new[] {0,1,-1}` per arm and an int[] per connection. updateVehicles calls these for every vehicle in a loaded chunk (up to VEHICLE_MAX=128) on every frame, so a rail network full of carts produces steady per-frame garbage.
findings.suggestedFix: Hoist the constant offset arrays into static readonly fields (BOAT_FW = {-0.8,0.8}, BOAT_SIDE = {-0.5,0.5}, CART_CORNERS, RAIL_DY = {0,1,-1,2,-2}, RAIL_CONN_DY = {0,1,-1}). Let railConnections fill a reusable static List<int[]> with preallocated int[3] entries; pickRailDirection copies the chosen values out right away, so a reused list is safe on the single main thread.

findings.jsRef: useBucketOrIgniter, pretty.js 19510-19513 (`if (left) { st.count++; return toast("Нет места для наполненного ведра"); }`); toast() at 25674 returns undefined
findings.description: When you fill a bucket from a stack of more than one and the inventory has no room, JS runs `return toast(...)`. toast() returns undefined, so useBucketOrIgniter returns a falsy value and placeBlock() keeps going: interactMobFeed, interactMobShear, useAxeStrip/useFarmItem/useHoe, eatSelected, and then `!isBK(s.key)` calls toast("В руке нет блока"). In JS the last message the player sees is therefore "В руке нет блока". The C# port returns true, so placeBlock stops early and shows "Нет места для наполненного ведра". The toast text and the rest of the placeBlock flow differ from JS.
findings.suggestedFix: To match JS exactly, change that branch to `{ st.count++; toast("Нет места для наполненного ведра"); return false; }` so placeBlock continues as it does in JS. If keeping the clearer message on purpose, list it as an intentional deviation.

findings.description: buildWorldDropBatches runs every frame. For every visible drop it calls dropLight -> getWorldLight (Render/VF.EntityModels.cs:170), which allocates a new double[2] each call. findings.jsRef: JS Map/Set iteration semantics (used by worldSim queues, chests/furnaces, blockMeta, etc.)
findings.description: The header comment says entries added during iteration are visited, but Delete() unlinks the node, so the tail moves back to n.prev. A Set() after that links the new node from n.prev, not from the deleted node n. An enumerator parked on n follows n.next, which is still null, and ends without visiting the new entry. Clear() during iteration has the same problem. Example: map {a}; foreach: at 'a' call Delete("a") then Set("b",..). A JS Map visits 'b'; OrderedMap ends after 'a'. This also applies to a chain of deleted trailing nodes. I found no current caller that does delete-then-add inside a foreach (the water queues snapshot first), so this is a latent semantic gap in a core helper.
findings.suggestedFix: Record removed nodes whose next was null when they were deleted (a small 'deadTail' list, or one pointer per chain). When Set() appends, point each of them at the new node: deadTail.next = n. After Clear(), make the old removed chain forward to the new head the same way. Or use lazy deletion: mark the node removed and unlink it only when no enumerator is active (count active enumerators with try/finally in GetEnumerator).

findings.description: setItem writes key.json.tmp, then File.Delete(f), then File.Move(tmp, f). If the process is killed, crashes or loses power between the Delete and the Move, the only copy left is the .tmp file. getItem never looks at .tmp, so the next launch sees the key as missing. Hitting the world 'edits'/'state'/'seed' keys loses the save, and for the seed key loadOrCreateWorldSeed then makes a new random seed, which regenerates the world. Saves run every 300 ms (saveGameSoon) and during OnApplicationQuit/OnApplicationPause, so the window is hit often.
findings.suggestedFix: When f exists, use File.Replace(tmp, f, null) (atomic on NTFS and POSIX). When it does not, use File.Move. In getItem, if f is missing but f+".tmp" exists, recover it by moving it into place and reading it.

findings.description: getItem swallows every exception from File.Exists/ReadAllText, adds the key to 'missing' and returns null, the same as 'key absent'. A transient read failure (file locked by antivirus or a cloud-sync client, a sharing violation) is then cached for the whole session. Traced effect: loadOrCreateWorldSeed sees r == null, makes a random seed and setItem overwrites the real seed file. loadGame sees no state, gives the starter inventory, and the next saveStateNow overwrites the real state. JS localStorage cannot fail this way.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a key to 'missing' only when File.Exists returns false. On an IOException, retry a few times with short sleeps. If it still fails, do not cache anything and surface the error (log it, and stop callers from overwriting, for example by throwing so the seed and state paths skip their regenerate-and-write).

findings.jsRef: Number.prototype.toString / toFixed (used where JS does String(x), x.toFixed(n))
findings.description: JS.ToStr and JS.Fixed do not match JS number formatting. Verified with Mono 6.8. Fixed uses .NET 'F' rounding, which rounds the 15-digit decimal: 1.005 gives "1.01" (JS toFixed(2) gives "1.00"), 2.675 gives "2.68" (JS "2.67"), -0.001 gives "0.00" (JS "-0.00"). ToStr uses "R" for anything outside |x|<1e15 integers: 0.00001 gives "1E-05" (JS "0.00001"), 1e-7 gives "1E-07" (JS "1e-7"), 1e15 gives "1E+15" (JS "1000000000000000"). Json.WriteNum (Json.cs:197) has the same issue for integers of 9e15 and above and for small decimals. These values show up in the debug HUD (VF.Frame.cs:127), the render-scale label and the world list spawn coordinates.
findings.suggestedFix: ToStr: print integers below 1e21 in full ("0" format on a decimal or BigInteger). For other values, take the shortest round-trip digits ("R") and re-layout them with JS rules: fixed notation when the decimal exponent is between -7 and 21 (exclusive), otherwise lowercase 'e' with an explicit sign and no zero padding. Fixed: format from the exact decimal value of the double (new decimal(v) when |v|<7.9e28), round half-up on that exact value, and keep the '-' sign for negative values that round to zero.

findings.jsRef: craftGridRecipe / recipeFits / canCraft (pretty.js 7663, 6613-6621), called by renderCraftGrid/renderRecipeBook only on UI re-render
findings.description: In JS these run once per UI re-render. In the port, IMGUI calls them on every OnGUI event: Layout, Repaint and mouse events, several times per frame while the inventory is open. Each craftGridRecipe call scans about 350 RECIPES and allocates `new bool[arr.Length]` for every shapeless rule (line 876) and `new[] { false, true }` / `new[] { false }` for every shaped rule (line 889). With the recipe book open, canCraft runs twice per recipe per event. Every craftable recipe goes through recipeFits → cloneInventory (LINQ Select/ToArray plus 36 Stack clones). Together this is hundreds to thousands of short-lived allocations per frame, plus Regex work in ingredientMatches (isPlankInventoryKey/woodFamilyForInventoryKey), which causes steady GC spikes while the inventory UI is open.
findings.suggestedFix: Use static readonly bool[] MIRROR_BOTH = {false,true}, MIRROR_ONE = {false}, and one reusable 'taken' buffer cleared with Array.Clear. In recipeFits, copy into a reusable static Stack[36] scratch buffer of reusable Stack objects instead of cloneInventory(). Optionally cache craftGridRecipe/canCraft results keyed on an inventory/grid revision counter that is bumped whenever inventoryDirty is set.

findings.description: audioPaused() checks `!Application.isFocused && Application.runInBackground == false`. VoxelForgeGame.Awake always sets Application.runInBackground = true, so this clause is always false. On desktop, minimizing or hiding the game never pauses audio, and since the simulation keeps running, sounds such as explosions and mob hits keep playing. JS suspends the AudioContext whenever document.hidden is true.
findings.suggestedFix: Track visibility in a static flag set from OnApplicationFocus/OnApplicationPause (for example appHidden = !focus || paused) and use `appHidden || pauseOpen || (player != null && player.sleeping)`. syncAudioState is already called from both callbacks.

findings.description: Every sound effect is synthesized synchronously on the main thread, with new buffers on every call. playSamples/applyReverbSend allocate buf, wet and four comb-delay lines, plus a new AudioClip. expRamp/envAt call Math.Pow per sample. sfxExplosion renders about 1.32 s of noise plus 1.2 s of tone (around 120k samples at 48 kHz), roughly 1 MB of float arrays and two Math.Pow calls per sample. A TNT chain fires many explosions in one frame, which produces multi-millisecond main-thread hitches and large GC spikes. WebAudio does this work off-thread in JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Precompute and cache clips (or per-material/per-preset buffers with a few randomized variants) on first use and play them with randomized pitch, or synthesize on a worker thread and only create/SetData the AudioClip on the main thread. Reuse scratch buffers (wet, delay lines) between calls. Replace the per-sample Math.Pow in expRamp with an incremental multiplicative ramp.

findings.jsRef: #pause z-index:15 vs #settingsUI/#modsUI z-index:30 (HTML CSS); openSettingsUI/openModsUI pretty.js 25972/26006; reset confirm() pretty.js 27183
findings.description: drawUI draws the layers bottom to top (pause, then settings, mods, death, dialog) in one OnGUI pass. In IMGUI the control drawn first gets MouseDown/MouseUp first and uses the event, so the pause buttons underneath take clicks meant for the panels drawn over them. The DOM modals are separate full-screen layers (z-index 30, or a native confirm()), so the pause screen gets no clicks while they are open. Traced at H=900 UI units. Pause row 1 is at y 429..463, row 2 ('Моды' / 'Выбор режима') at 471..505, row 3 ('Сбросить мир') at 513..547. In Settings, the Sound toggle (y 427..449, x from W/2-120) lies on top of 'Продолжить': clicking the checkbox resumes the game (hidePause + pointer lock) with Settings still open, and the setting does not change. The dynamic-resolution toggle (491..513) lies on top of 'Моды' and 'Выбор режима': clicking its label calls returnToTitle(). In the 'Сбросить мир' confirm dialog, OK (x W/2-8..W/2+92, y 482..514) and 'Отмена' (W/2+102..W/2+202) both lie on top of 'Выбор режима', so either button quits to the title screen and leaves the dialog and its reset callback pending. On the start screen, the delete/copy dialog buttons lie on top of the 'Играть' and 'Копия' buttons of the 4th visible world row: confirming a delete can start another world, and confirming the copy alert makes one more copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the top-most modal the only layer that receives input. Compute the top layer first (dialog > death > mods/settings > gameUI > pause > HUD/start). For every layer below it, draw only on Repaint, or wrap it in GUI.enabled=false (restore afterwards). For example, `bool modal = dialogText != null; bool overPause = settingsOpen || modsOpen;`, then draw the pause screen with GUI.enabled = !(modal || overPause) and the start screen and world list with GUI.enabled = !modal. Another option is to use GUI.ModalWindow for the dialog.

findings.jsRef: keydown/keyup listeners pretty.js 26203-26277 (no focus gating; Escape always handled)
findings.description: While uiTextFocused is true, pollInput skips every key: KeyDown and KeyUp, Escape and E included. uiTextFocused is GUIUtility.keyboardControl != 0 while the start screen is up or the recipe book is open. In runtime IMGUI, GUI.Button, Toggle and Slider are FocusType.Passive and clicking elsewhere does not remove TextField focus. So once the player clicks into the recipe search field, Escape and E stop working for the rest of the time the inventory is open; it can only be closed with the 'Закрыть' button. The JS window keydown handler always handles Escape (closeGameUI). Dropped KeyUp events also leave keys stuck. Example: hold W in the inventory, click the search field, release W. keys keeps 'KeyW', closeGameUI does not clear it and pointer-lock acquisition does not call clearInputState, so the player walks forward by itself after re-locking. recipeBookOpen persists, and keyboardControl is never reset by the code, so a stale focus id can block keys the next time the inventory is opened.
findings.suggestedFix: Always process KeyUp, whatever the focus. Always process Escape, and when it arrives with a field focused, also clear focus (GUIUtility.keyboardControl = 0). Compute uiTextFocused from the focused control's name (GUI.GetNameOfFocusedControl() is "worldName" or "recipeSearch") and only while that field is actually drawn this frame. Clear focus on any MouseDown that is not inside a text field: in drawUI, before the layers, `if (e.type==MouseDown) GUIUtility.keyboardControl = 0;` and let the TextField re-take it. Also set keyboardControl = 0 in openGameUI and closeGameUI.

findings.description: On touch devices Unity sends each touch both to Input.touches, which pollTouch reads in Update, and to IMGUI as a simulated MouseDown in the same frame's OnGUI. Tapping the inventory button calls openGameUI() in Update, so that frame's OnGUI already draws the inventory and gives it the same MouseDown at the button's position (bottom-right, which is inside the right panel). If the tap lands on the creative palette, the item is picked at once on MouseDown and replaces the selected hotbar slot. If it lands on a slot, drag state is set and the MouseUp at touch end runs slotLeftClick, which picks the stack up into the cursor. In JS, preventDefault() on pointerdown stops the gesture from reaching the newly shown UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Ignore IMGUI mouse events that come from a touch that began while gameplay touch was active. For example, record the frame in which pollTouch opened UI or pause (uiOpenedByTouchFrame = Time.frameCount) and skip MouseDown/MouseUp in drawGameUI for that touch until all touches have ended. Alternatively, set Input.simulateMouseWithTouches=false and feed IMGUI from touches yourself.

findings.jsRef: drawHotbar el.onpointerdown (TOUCH_DEVICE) pretty.js 26350-26357; #gameUI,#deathUI,... inset:0 z-index:30 pointer-events:auto
findings.description: The touch hotbar handler in drawHUD runs whenever the HUD is drawn, including while the inventory, pause or death screen is open. It runs before drawGameUI and calls Event.current.Use(). On short screens the inventory panel (wh = min(720, H-24), centred) covers the hotbar rect (H-58..H-12). Example: H=400, the panel's bottom inventory row is at about y 308..354 and the hotbar at 342..388. A tap there selects a hotbar slot and the inventory slot never sees the event. In JS the full-screen #gameUI/#deathUI overlay takes these pointer events, so the hotbar cannot be tapped while a UI is open. pollTouch also treats a hotbar tap as the start of a camera look (p.x > 0.35*W), so dragging on the hotbar turns the camera.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle the hotbar tap only when touchGameplayEnabled() (or at least when !uiOpen && !pauseOpen && !player.dead), or block lower layers as in UI-1. In pollTouch, do not start a look touch when the finger begins inside the hotbar rect.

findings.description: A browser double-click fires click, click, dblclick. The port runs slotDoubleClick on the second MouseDown (clickCount==2) and drops that second click's left-click action. The result differs whenever the first click swaps the cursor with the slot. Example: cursor holds Y, slot holds X. In JS the two clicks swap twice (slot X, cursor Y) and dblclick then collects Y items into the cursor. In C# only one swap happens (slot Y, cursor X) and X items are collected. With armor (single) slots this leaves the wrong piece equipped.
findings.suggestedFix: On MouseDown with clickCount==2, set a pendingDouble flag and keep the drag state. On the matching MouseUp, run slotLeftClick(arr,i,opts,e.shift) first, then slotDoubleClick(arr,i), which matches the JS event order.

findings.description: drawRecipeBook runs on every OnGUI event: Layout, Repaint and every mouse move or drag, so at least twice per frame. Each time it calls canCraft(rec) twice per recipe (lines 556 and 566), and each call runs countItem plus recipeFits → cloneInventory + removeItem simulation. It also rebuilds and lower-cases the 'hay' string and recipeNeedTextUI per recipe. With a few hundred RECIPES (block/virtual recipes are added in a loop), that is thousands of inventory clones and many strings per frame while the book is open, which causes steady GC churn. JS rebuilds the list only when renderCurrentUI is called.
findings.suggestedFix: Cache the filtered list together with each recipe's ok flag. Recompute only when the inventory, the search text, the filter or the mode changes (for example a version counter bumped wherever inventoryDirty is set), or at most once per frame on EventType.Layout, and reuse it for Repaint and input events.

findings.description: drawStartScreen calls ensureLegacyWorldIndex() on every OnGUI event. That re-parses the world index JSON from LocalStorage, runs legacyWorldExists for both modes, and builds a LINQ OrderByDescending list plus per-row meta strings (with string.Join/Select and DateTime formatting) several times per frame. JS renders the list only when it changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Cache the sorted world list. Invalidate it after create, copy, delete and returnToTitle, or re-read it at most once per frame on EventType.Layout.

findings.description: resetTouchMove returns early when !TOUCH_DEVICE. In JS it always clears KeyW/A/S/D/Space/ShiftLeft and sprintLatch. On desktop, syncTouchControls() (on = false) runs on every showPause/hidePause/openGameUI/closeGameUI/startGame, so JS clears movement keys and the sprint latch at every pause or UI transition, for example when pointer lock is regained (hidePause) and when the inventory closes. In the port, movement keys or sprintLatch that went stale while a UI was open (see UI-2) survive these transitions.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the `if (!TOUCH_DEVICE) return;` line so that the key and sprintLatch clearing always runs, as in JS.

findings.jsRef: #tip CSS: top:14px centred, hidden at max-width:700px or pointer:coarse; #mode right/top; #toast top:70px; #xrayBadge right:12px bottom:250px
findings.description: The controls tip is drawn at the bottom-left (y = H-26, width W-20). It runs straight through the hotbar (y H-58..H-12, x W/2-215..W/2+215) and overlaps the slot icons and counts on any desktop width. In JS it is a top-centred pill, hidden below 700px width. Other HUD elements are also moved: modeText sits under the stats on the left (JS: top-right), the toast is at 0.28*H (JS: top 70px), the X-RAY badge is at top-centre (JS: bottom-right above the minimap), and the mine bar is 160px wide (JS: 92px).
findings.suggestedFix: Draw the tip top-centred (y≈14) inside a translucent box and hide it when W <= 700. Place modeText top-right, the toast at y=70, the xray badge at right:12 / bottom:250 (205 on small screens), and make the mine bar 92x7, matching the CSS.

findings.description: World names, which the player types freely (up to 40 characters), are drawn through styles with richText=true and wrapped in …. They are also concatenated into the dialog texts at lines 164 and 166. A name such as 'X' or '' is read as markup, which breaks the row layout. JS sets them with textContent, so the text is always literal.
findings.suggestedFix: Draw user-supplied names with a style that has richText=false (draw the bold header separately), or escape '<' (for example replace it with '<​') before concatenating.

findings.jsRef: renderModsUI <label class=modRow> wrapping checkbox pretty.js 25984-25996; renderCreativePalette el.title pretty.js 7292
findings.description: In JS each mod row is a <label> that wraps the checkbox, so clicking the mod name or description toggles it. The port makes only a 24x24 toggle clickable; clicks on the text do nothing, or hit the pause buttons underneath (UI-1). The creative palette items also have no hover name: JS sets el.title = d.name, and the port draws no tooltip for palette cells at line 501.

results.reason: Confirmed. `line` is a reserved HLSL keyword (a geometry-shader primitive type), so fxc/HLSLcc reject `float line = ...`. In VFTerrainXray.shader I renamed the local to `edgeLine` in its declaration, the discard test and the alpha output; the maths is unchanged. I also scanned the other shaders and VFCommon.cginc for reserved words and found no other collisions.

Confirmed. JS drawEntities (pretty.js 3446) disables DEPTH_TEST in X-Ray mode, and a disabled depth test writes no depth. The port's ZWrite On made X-Ray mobs write depth. VFEntity.shader now has `_ZWrite ("ZWrite", Float) = 1` and uses `ZWrite [_ZWrite]`. The default 1 keeps matEntity as it was. The behaviour fix itself needs one line in VF.Renderer.cs, which I do not own (see crossFileIssues).

Confirmed. Global depthFunc is LESS (pretty.js 1100), and every LEQUAL change is set back to LESS (27054->27057 for the water colour pass, and also 15397->15410), so the function is LESS when drawMainClouds runs at 27062. VFCloud.shader changed from ZTest LEqual to ZTest Less.

Change to `matEntityXray = mk("VoxelForge/Entity", m => { m.mainTexture = entityTex; m.SetFloat("_ZTest", (float)CompareFunction.Always); m.SetFloat("_ZWrite", 0); });`. results.reason: Confirmed. In JS, drawEntities calls gl.disable(DEPTH_TEST) in X-ray mode, and in GL that also stops depth writes. VFEntity.shader already has the _ZWrite property and uses ZWrite [_ZWrite], so no shader change was needed. matEntityXray now also calls m.SetFloat("_ZWrite", 0) (VF.Renderer.cs initRenderer).

Confirmed. chunkRenderRegionKey builds a string with int boxing for every visible chunk on every frame. Added a cached key on the Chunk (_rrKey, plus the cx/cz it was built from) and chunkRenderRegionKeyCached(c) in VF.ChunkRender.cs. buildOpaqueRenderList now uses the cache, so the hot path makes no allocations. The renderRegions dictionary is unchanged, so the Clear() in VF.Frame.cs stays consistent.

Confirmed. Ties in _renderDist2 are common: hd2 is the distance to the nearest edge, so mirrored left/right offsets give equal values. List.Sort is an unstable introsort, while JS Array.sort is stable. Replaced it with sortByRenderDist in VF.Renderer.cs: stable, no allocations, insertion-sorted runs of 16 followed by a bottom-up merge using static scratch arrays, which are cleared afterwards. The comparison matches JS, ascending by _renderDist2 with the left element kept first on ties.

Confirmed. SetVertexBufferParams and SetIndexBufferParams were called with exact counts on every frame, and the quad and sequential index patterns were re-uploaded every frame. DynMesh now grows its vertex and index capacity only when needed, by doubling. For quads the vertex capacity is at least quadIndexCap*4, so every resident index is in range. The static index pattern is uploaded only when its capacity grows (tracked by idxUploaded, which the explicit-index Upload resets). Vertices go up with a partial SetVertexBufferData, and SetSubMesh(0, ic, firstVertex 0, vertexCount vn) draws only the used range. A quad batch with fewer than 4 vertices now returns false instead of recording a 0-index draw; the visible result is the same.

Confirmed. recycleMesh pooled up to 256 meshes with their vertex and index buffers still allocated. Checked that clearing is safe: every freeMesh/freeRegionMesh call happens in frameSimulate (stream, pumpRenderRegionBuilds), which runs before renderWorld records frameCB, never between recording and the camera render. Shared-region views are guarded by ensureChunk*ViewCurrent, which checks r.mesh != null and the generation. recycleMesh now calls m.Clear() before pushing to the pool. writeTerrainMesh sets the buffer params, submeshes and bounds again on reuse.

results.reason: Confirmed. ensureShipTables() filled four static tables lazily with plain stores and checked SHIP_ALL != null without any barrier. Several VF-Gen kernels and the main-thread WORLDGEN kernel call it concurrently through structureCandidate, so on weakly ordered hardware a thread could see SHIP_ALL non-null while the prefix arrays still read as null. Fix in WorldGenKernel.Structures.cs: the fast path now uses Volatile.Read(ref SHIP_ALL). Building happens under a static lock with a second check inside it. The three companion tables are stored first and SHIP_ALL is published last with Volatile.Write. Table contents and order are unchanged.

Confirmed as a real allocation hot path; the output matched JS. Each lookup in planRavine, ravinesForChunk, planMineshaft, mineshaftsForChunk and structureCandidate built a string and boxed its ints. The seed prefix adds nothing because setSeed clears every cache whenever the seed changes, and these caches are only looked up, never iterated. Changes: (1) The caches are now Dictionary<long,...> keyed by xzKey(x,z) = ((long)x<<32)|(uint)z. They use a mixing IEqualityComparer<long> (XZKeyCmp), because long.GetHashCode is lo^hi and collides heavily on nearby grid cells. (2) structureCache is now one long-keyed dictionary per structure type, selected by a new StructCfg.idx field. This replaces the salt in the JS key, and setSeed clears all four. (3) surfaceStructureReservedAt now runs the nearbyStructures loop inline without allocating a List. It still evaluates every candidate of a type in the same order before returning, so the sequence of structureCandidate, biome and surface calls, and with it the climateLastLeaf state, stays identical. The size-cap clears and the hit != null check in mineshaftsForChunk are kept.

results.reason: The finding is real: in full mode, run() calls take() for each section, which allocates new arrays and worldifies them, and then concat() copies everything again into aggO/C/W/T. So every vertex and index is allocated and copied twice. JS avoids this with subarray views. It cannot be fixed inside MeshCore/MeshTypes alone. GeoBucket's contract (v.Length == VCount, indices start at 0 in its own array) is read directly by VF.ChunkRender.cs (makeMesh/updateMeshBuffers/writeTerrainMesh, the region Array.Copy(g.v,0,..), setChunkWaterCPU, the water sort) and by VF.Workers.cs (bucketEqual, combineSectionBucket). Section buckets in full24 must also stay separate arrays because Workers keeps them as c.sectionGeo for later partial remeshes. A view-based GeoBucket needs coordinated changes in those files. No change was made.

Confirmed: these per-block heap allocations were real. Fixes in MeshCore.cs, each producing the same output as before. (1) stairBoxesMain: the Func closures metaAt/isStair/guard are replaced by the private methods stairAt/stairGuard, which call vmeta directly. The base slab and the step/corner boxes come from a static STAIR_STEP[up][kind][dir] table built once with rotateBox (dir = faceIndexForFacing(facing), the same mapping rotateBox uses). vStairBoxes uses the same table. (2) emitRail: the slope lambda is replaced by static railUp(d,px,pz) with the same expressions. (3) shapeBoxes, vShapeBoxes and connectBoxes: fixed shapes are static readonly arrays (slab, trapdoor, open trapdoor rotated x4, carpet, plate, bamboo, pot, bed, fence/wall/pane posts, gate posts/rails/open rails, sea pickles). They are returned through a reusable per-instance boxScratch list. The callers (buildSection, emitVirtualBlock) only iterate it immediately and never nest calls, and boxPart/vBox only read the arrays. Gate branches add elements explicitly rather than with AddRange, which can allocate a temporary array on Mono. workerButtonBox still allocates one small array per button, which is minor. (4) flushFlatWaterTops: the group lists and key dictionary are pooled per instance (flatGroups/flatGroupIdx, with gn as the live count). First-seen group order and the merge are unchanged.

results.reason: Confirmed. returnToTitle() calls saveGameNow() and then clearRuntimeWorld(), and clearRuntimeWorld() never cancelled saveTimer. Timers keep ticking on the title screen, so a pending 300 ms scheduleWorldSave would later call saveWorldNow() with the old SAVE_KEYS and empty edits/meta, wiping the save. Fix: clearRuntimeWorld() in World/VF.World.cs now starts with `Timers.clearTimeout(saveTimer); saveTimer = 0;`. This is also safe from the loadWorldSave() call path, because no world save is pending when a new world loads. The matching saveGameT problem in VF.Inventory.cs is listed in crossFileIssues.

Confirmed. spawnWorldDrop does worldDrops.Add (VF.Drops.cs:21), and detachUnsupportedAt calls it in survival (VF.BlockRules.cs:453/468). The C# foreach over that List<WorldDrop> would throw 'Collection was modified', where JS for-of over a growing array keeps going. Fix: in tickPressurePlates (World/VF.WorldTick.cs) the liveMobs and worldDrops loops now go by index, the same way JS for-of walks an array. The pressurePlateActive loop keeps its snapshot, because any entry added during the loop has an until time later than now and is skipped anyway.

Fixes in World/VF.WorldTick.cs: (1) snapshotSimMap now returns a shared, read-only empty list when the map is empty, so the common per-frame case allocates nothing. All callers only foreach over the result. (2) tickFurnaces now uses snapshotSimMap(furnaces), the same OrderedMap<string,Furnace> type, so an empty furnace map allocates nothing. The furnace UI-refresh code after the loop still runs, as in JS. (3) tickFallingBlocks replaced OrderBy(...).ToList() with an in-place stable insertion sort on y. That matches JS Array.sort((a,b)=>a.y-b.y), which is stable, and costs about O(n) because the list stays nearly sorted between frames. I did not use reusable scratch lists for non-empty snapshots: a C# foreach over a list that is cleared mid-loop by a nested snapshot would throw, so a fresh list stays the safe choice there.

results.reason: Confirmed. When a tail node was deleted during iteration, its next stayed null and a later Set linked the new node from n.prev, so a parked enumerator stopped early. Clear() had the same gap. Fix in Ordered.cs: removed nodes whose next was the list end go into a deadTails list (Delete of the tail adds it, and Clear adds the old tail). Set() points each dead tail at the newly appended node and empties the list. Tested with Mono: delete-then-add gives 'ab', chained tail deletes give 'ade', clear-then-add gives 'ax', and re-adding a deleted key gives 'aba', all matching JS Map.

Confirmed: Delete+Move leaves a window where only key.json.tmp exists, and getItem ignored it. setItem now writes the tmp file, then calls File.Move when the target is missing or File.Replace(tmp, f, null) when it exists. It falls back to Delete+Move only if Replace throws. getItem moves an orphaned .tmp into place when the main file is missing. removeItem also deletes a leftover .tmp so a removed key cannot come back. File.Replace was checked on Mono: atomic, tmp consumed.

Confirmed: any IO exception was cached as 'missing' for the whole session, and the seed/state paths then regenerated their data and overwrote the real files. getItem now caches 'missing' only when File.Exists is false. It retries the read 4 times with short sleeps (10/30/50 ms), never caches a failure, and logs an error. A key that keeps failing to read goes into a readFailed set. setItem refuses to overwrite such a key while its file still exists, so the real save survives; it logs a warning instead. A later successful read, or removeItem, clears the flag. No caller changes were needed: callers still just see null, as in JS.

Confirmed. Rewrote JS.ToStr(double) to match JS Number::toString: shortest round-trip digits plus JS fixed/exponent layout (lowercase e with explicit sign, fixed notation for exponent -7 < n <= 21) and NaN/Infinity. Integers below 2^53 keep the fast path. I did not use the reviewer's 'print integers below 1e21 in full', which is wrong above 2^53: JS prints 2**60 as 1152921504606847000. Mono's double.Parse turned out not to be correctly rounded, so the round-trip check does not use it. The fast path is exact: the 15-digit rounding N, checked with N*10^q, which is a single IEEE operation and exact for N < 2^53, |q| <= 22. Otherwise it falls back to an exact check of the rounding interval with base-1e9 big integers (bigDec/bigMul/bigCmp). JS.Fixed now rounds half-up on the exact binary value of the double: a guarded double fast path, else exact digits from bigDec. It keeps '-' for small negatives (-0.001 gives '-0.00') and returns ToStr for values of 1e21 and above. Json.WriteNum now uses JS.ToStr (same rules as JSON.stringify). Checked with Node against about 140k values (fixed edge cases, random magnitudes, random bit patterns, subnormals, MAX_VALUE) for toString and toFixed(0,1,2,3,5,12), compared from exact bit patterns: 0 mismatches. Cost is about 3 us per ToStr call and 0.5 us per Fixed call.
